# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Precious metals prices generally firmed in the last week of November. Continuing worries about Europe placed some upwards pressure on the gold price despite a degree of Dollar strength. The other precious metals could not gain any ground from the 22nd to the 29th as investors fretted about the outlook for global economic growth. The main change in sentiment came on the 30th of November when a range of Central Banks coordinated their actions to inject liquidity into the world’s economic system. All of the metals reacted positively but palladium and gold gained most. Looking forwards, the next risk event that the market is looking at is the EU summit on the 9th of November and trading could be quiet until then. • There were no clear trends across the precious metals futures markets in the final week of November, in contrast to the previous week’s price driven long liquidation. Gold and platinum saw little change in interest but investors added to their short positions in silver and palladium, something they may well have regretted as the prices of these two metals moved higher after the concerted Central Bank activity of last week. • There was a disconnect between the activities of ETF investors in the platinum group metals and those holding gold and silver. Platinum and palladium saw heavy net selling suggesting that investors still remain extremely worried about the prospect of recession or turgid growth in most of the developed world. Gold and silver saw relatively gentle net buying interest as the Euro debt crisis moves towards the next summit meeting and risk event. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **05 December 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **05 December 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 29 November 2011; ETF data to 2 December 2011.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

A general sense of fear persisted in the markets and this led to gold buying despite the sharp fall in the price of the previous week. Gold rebounded to break $1,700 on the 23rd following the news that the US Supercommittee could not come to any agreement over cost-cutting. The undersubscription of a German bond issue also drove some nervous gold buying but weakened the Euro, sending gold lower instead, to $1,680 on the 23rd and the 25th. However, on the 28th, the Dollar stopped firming and weakened instead even as rumours started flying that French sovereign debt might be downgraded. Gold jumped to $1,720 that day. The real news, though, came on the 30th, when a number of Central Banks announced a coordinated action to improve liquidity in the global financial markets. Almost every asset reacted positively and gold leapt to $1,745 where it ended the month. With another EU summit ahead on Friday, trading could be quieter this week. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—November 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- After the previous week’s selling, the last week of November saw a little futures buying for gold. Net long speculative positions on COMEX climbed by 259,000 ounces to 21.4 million ounces. TOCOM positions slipped 10,000 ounces lower but there was little clear appetite for increasing long exposure to gold amongst futures investors. - Gold ETF holdings have now risen for eight consecutive weeks, during which period they have increased from 67.1 million ounces to 70.3 million ounces. - Silver followed gold in the final week of November but proved unable to challenge the highs of recent weeks, with much bearish sentiment present in the market. On the 22nd, silver jumped from $31.50 to a high of $33 following the Supercommittee’s admission of failure in its mission to agree on steps towards reducing the US budget deficit. The high was short-lived though, with silver tumbling back to $31.50 on the following day and slipping to a low of just above $31 on the 25th. The dollar started to soften, however, allowing gold to move higher and drag silver with it, rescuing it from this bearish trend. The price recovered to $32 on the 28th but, once again, it drifted lower to below $31.50 on the 30th before the Central Bank announcement of additional liquidity injections. It roared higher, to $32.90 on the 30th. Investors have since made an effort to drive silver through $33.50 but these attempts were unconvincing and silver is currently trading below $33. - Net long speculative interest in silver

on COMEX fell by 4.4 million ounces in the last week of November as the previous week’s price fall drove a few more investors to add to short positions in contrast to the previous week when long investors had been forced to liquidate some very large positions. Sentiment remains unconvincing though, with positioning at only 129 million ounces on COMEX. - Silver ETF flows continue to fluctuate, with this week seeing buying of 2.86 million ounces, almost exactly reversing the previous week’s net selling. The recent move higher in the silver price can be expected to attract more ETF buying this week. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **05 December 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 29 November 2011; ETF data to 2 December 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Platinum was the least positive of the precious metals in price terms in the final week of November. While the other metals all gained ground, platinum stayed fairly level. Worryingly, even a rising gold price had no impact with the gold-platinum spread widening from $130 an ounce to almost $200. This suggests that price appreciation for platinum may be harder-won in coming weeks than the market might expect. Reasonable sales volumes on the Shanghai Gold Exchange were balanced by very strong ETF selling, leaving platinum with no clear momentum. It traded between roughly $1,570 and a s

hort-lived low of $1,515 (on the 30th). The price trend is clearly bearish but Central Bank action on the 30th provided a considerable boost, suggesting that any movement towards a resolution of the European crisis could be positive for the platinum price. - There was little to say of note about the platinum futures markets in the last week of November. Net long speculative positions were almost unchanged at just under 1.4 million ounces for TOCOM and NYMEX combined. However, platinum maintained investor interest rather better than palladium as its clearer link to the gold price proved attractive. - The week to the 2nd of November saw ferocious selling of platinum from the ETFs with a net outflow of 70,800 ounces being the heaviest selling since August 2008 and the second largest outflow since these funds were launched. Selling was seen in some of the larger funds and on both sides of the Atlantic and seems to have been driven by the previous week’s price decline. Holdings now stand at 1.41 million ounces. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **05 December 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 29 November 2011; ETF data to 2 December 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

For the last week of November, it weakened, along with platinum, slipping gradually from $590 on the 22nd to $565 on the 25th. On the 23rd, it did break $600 but palladium could not hold this level for long amidst investor selling of ETF metal and growing short futures positions. The price flickered briefly higher on the 28th but failed to break $600, before falling back to $570 on the 30th. However, the Central Bank announcement on the 30th drove all of the metals higher in a risk-on move. Palladium shot through $600 and forced short covering, adding more energy to the move. Positive sales data from the North American automotive market contributed more momentum at the start of December and palladium reached $660 on the 2nd, a remarkable recovery. However, with ETF disinvestment still being seen and global ec

onomic growth apparently slow, some selling pressure may be seen in the coming week. Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—November 11

• The last week of November saw more futures selling from investors with net long speculative positions crashing another 62,000 ounces on NYMEX to 523,000 ounces. Those who added to their short positions must have rued their decision when palladium shot higher at the end of the week, forcing short covering which should be revealed in next week’s figures. - The week to the 2nd of December saw ETF investors continue their selling of palladium. 54,000 ounces more were sold than were bought and positions fell to 1.8 million ounces, almost half a million ounces lower than at the start of the year. With net flows of metal so volatile, following last year’s heavy buying, it has become more difficult for shorter term investors to focus on this metal’s underlying fundamentals. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** #### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
